---
title: "Select groups of predictors"
description: "Predictor groups, parameter-count information criteria and comparisons with grpreg."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment='#>',message=FALSE,warning=FALSE)
```

A categorical predictor can require several contrasts, and a smooth effect can
require several spline coefficients. The `group` argument selects such terms
together. It also supports groups of related measurements. Adaptive ridge uses
the squared Euclidean norm of the coefficients within each group, so positive
and negative effects contribute equally to selection. The adaptive exponent
is fixed at $\gamma=2$.

## Fit and tune grouped predictors

```{r grouped-fit}
library(L0glm)
set.seed(41)
X <- matrix(rnorm(200*12),200,12)
group <- rep(1:6,each=2)
group[11:12] <- 0
beta <- c(1.5,-1.5,0,0,1,-1,rep(0,6))
y <- 1+as.numeric(X%*%beta)+rnorm(200)
fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,group=group,intercept=TRUE,lambda='gic',relaxed=TRUE)
l0glmMetrics(fit)[c('gic','group_support_size','group_df')]
```

Group labels can be integers, characters or factors in any order. Group `0`,
the intercept and `always.include` terms are unpenalized. Explicit starting-zero
exclusions remain binding; the returned sparse coefficient matrix retains all
original predictor rows. A relaxed refit removes shrinkage on the retained groups.

For multiple outcomes, `grouped=FALSE` selects each predictor group independently
within each channel. `grouped=TRUE` pools its coefficients across channels.
Joint multinomial fits pool the identifiable CLR coefficients across categories.

```{r grouped-cv, eval=FALSE}
cv <- l0glmTune(X,y,family=gaussian(),group=group,intercept=TRUE,relaxed=TRUE,
  tune='cv',nfolds=5,nlambda=10)
predict(cv$fit_1se,X[1:5,])
```

Every CV training fold repeats selection independently. Automatic local refinement
tests whole-group additions, removals and exchanges when the initial selected
coefficient dimension is at most 50. See [predictor groups](../reference/predictor_groups.html)
for the penalty equations and [local refinement](../reference/local_search.html)
for its controls. Predictor-group models currently fit the supplied design directly;
use `screen='none'` when its dimensions would otherwise activate automatic ISIS.

Recognized scalar GLMs run predictor-group IRLS in C++, with the same group
penalties, step halving, dispersion updates and convergence checks. Multiple
outcomes can use OpenMP channel workers through `parallelize=TRUE, ncores=4`.
BLAS uses one thread within those parallel passes, and the caller's thread
settings are restored. Custom and special-family adapters and validation
checkpoints use the structured R driver.

## GIC and group size

The reported information criteria use the same parameter-count convention as
other L0glm models:

\[
\mathrm{GIC}=-2\ell(\widehat B,\widehat\psi)
  +\log(p)\log\log(n)\,k.
\]

Here $k$ counts free nonzero coefficients, compulsory coefficient dimensions and
estimated noise parameters. Multinomial counts respect the CLR zero-sum constraint.
The original selectable predictor count $p$ is retained. A selected group of four
unrestricted coefficients contributes four parameters; its size is accounted for
through those coefficients. No further group-size multiplier enters the reported
GIC. See [information criteria](../reference/information_criteria.html) for the
Fan–Tang GIC and its assumptions.

To calibrate adaptive-ridge block selection, named IC presets use nominal group
coefficient dimensions as penalty multipliers. Exact boundary zeros can reduce
the reported parameter count of the resulting fit. IC tuning and local refinement
evaluate that returned support using the parameter-count criterion above.
A numeric `lambda` instead specifies a penalty per selected group, with optional
`group.multiplier` values; `group_objective` reports this weighted group target.
Stored multipliers permit numerical reproduction of an IC-calibrated ridge fit.

Other group-specific selection criteria are possible. For example,
[Zhang et al.](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.2022.1241) study a group-count criterion
in Gaussian best-subset-of-groups regression. L0glm retains its parameter-count
GIC across families and uses it consistently in the comparisons below.

## Comparisons with grpreg

These four simulations include equal and unequal group sizes, correlated
predictors and signed effects. Each is repeated with three independent seeds.
Two compulsory predictors and an intercept are retained in every method.
The [reproduction script](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmark_predictor_groups.R)
compares L0glm with grpreg's group LASSO, group MCP and group SCAD, using both
information-criterion paths and five-fold CV with shared folds.

The GIC comparisons use one common likelihood and count active coefficients.
For Gaussian data the variance is known to be one, which makes the score
comparable even for nearly interpolating path fits. L0glm's estimated-scale
fits are included as a diagnostic alongside the known-scale fits. The grpreg
paths contain 40 lambda values; L0glm uses its GIC preset or a ten-value CV grid.
This common scoring choice is distinct from grpreg's default shrinkage-based
effective degrees of freedom, described in its
[selection documentation](https://pbreheny.github.io/grpreg/reference/select.html).

```{r group-results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
path <- '../../../benchmarks/plots/predictor-groups/summary.csv'
results <- read.csv(path)
for(case in c('gaussian_equal','gaussian_wide','logistic_equal','logistic_unequal')) {
  d <- results[results$case==case & results$tune!='5-fold CV',]
  d <- d[match(c('L0glm','L0glm estimated scale','grLasso','grMCP','grSCAD'),d$method),]
  d <- d[!is.na(d$method),]
  cat('\n\n**',gsub('_',' ',case),':** ',d$n[1],' observations, ',d$p[1],
    ' predictors, ',d$groups[1],' groups (',d$true_groups[1],' active).\n\n',sep='')
  table <- d[c('method','seconds','GIC','TP','FP','F1','MCC')]
  names(table) <- c('Method','Seconds','GIC','Group TP','Group FP','F1','MCC')
  print(knitr::kable(table,digits=c(0,2,1,2,2,3,3),row.names=FALSE))
}
```

Gaussian preset fits recover the groups accurately, with prediction errors close
to the noise level in the equal-size case. The native group driver reuses bounded
Gaussian weighted cross-products and runs the iteration in C++. Wide systems
retain the Woodbury solver path, and sparse inputs retain their sparse solves. In logistic
regression, L0glm's preset with local refinement
is faster than these complete paths; the unequal-size, correlated example is
harder for parameter-count GIC, and CV recovers more of its true groups.
For CV, grpreg's native group coordinate-descent paths reuse work through warm
starts along the lambda sequence. L0glm repeats independent adaptive-ridge fits
and whole-group local refinement within each training fold. Its preset avoids
that grid search when information-criterion selection is appropriate.

```{r cv-results, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
d <- results[results$tune=='5-fold CV',]
d <- d[order(match(d$case,c('gaussian_equal','gaussian_wide','logistic_equal','logistic_unequal')),
  match(d$method,c('L0glm','grLasso','grMCP','grSCAD'))),]
table <- d[c('case','method','seconds','TP','FP','F1','MCC')]
names(table) <- c('Simulation','Method','Seconds','Group TP','Group FP','F1','MCC')
knitr::kable(table,digits=c(0,0,2,2,2,3,3),row.names=FALSE)
```

Timings are medians; recovery scores are averages across three replicates.
All fits and CV folds use one thread, on an HP ZBook Fury G8 with an Intel
Core i9-11950H, Windows, R 4.5.0 and grpreg 3.6.0. Simulation and final scoring
are excluded from the timings; fitting and selection are included. For grpreg's
GIC paths this includes scoring all candidates with the common criterion.
The complete
[run-level results](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/L0glm/blob/master/benchmarks/plots/predictor-groups/runs.csv)
include test RMSE or AUC/log loss, convergence diagnostics and path warnings.
